title: A Team Exercise to Introduce New Best Practices
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note describes a concrete, repeatable team activity called the 'Best Practices Slide' exercise, in which every team member creates a one-page slide describing a practice they've encountered elsewhere -- from a former employer, a peer's workplace, or a case study -- and pitches it to the group in three minutes or less. The team then prioritizes the top practices and assigns champions to ensure implementation. The piece frames this as more valuable than purely entertaining team-building activities because it produces lasting operational improvements, recommending it as an annual ritual.
points: The 'Best Practices Slide' exercise has each team member pitch one external best practice on a single slide.
Sources for practices include former employers, peers' workplaces, case studies, or podcasts.
Presentations are capped at three minutes each, followed by group prioritization of the top practices.
Assigning a champion for each selected practice is recommended to ensure it actually gets implemented.
Run annually, the exercise is said to yield more than a dozen new best practices over time.
quotes: The best team exercises have a measurable long-term impact on the organization and culture.
The primary instruction for each team member is to create a one-page slide (maximum one side, one page) that explains a Best Practice they believe should be introduced and incorporated.
When the team gathers, each team member takes three minutes or less to persuasively present their Best Practice to the group.
Selecting a champion to make sure each Best Practice becomes a mainstay in the enterprise is also a good idea.
Do this exercise once a year, and over a span of time, you will find more than a dozen new Best Practices that can become part of how the team and organization operate more effectively.
